speaker: Samantha
text: Good morning everyone, and welcome back to the course on training neural networks.

speaker: Samantha
text: Today we are going to walk through a full training run, from the raw data to a model we can actually trust.

speaker: Samantha
text: Before we start, a quick word about logistics, because a few of you asked about the assignment.

speaker: Samantha
text: The deadline for the second assignment moves to Friday the fourteenth, so you have one extra week.

speaker: Samantha
text: Please submit through the usual portal, and keep your notebooks tidy.

speaker: Daniel
text: Thanks. Let me pick up with the data, since everything else depends on it.

speaker: Daniel
text: The dataset we use this term is called Meadowlark, and it contains about forty thousand labelled images of birds.

speaker: Daniel
text: Each image comes with a species label and a rough bounding box drawn by volunteers.

speaker: Daniel
text: We hold out one in every five images for validation and never touch them during training.

speaker: Daniel
text: The labels are noisy, so expect some birds to be filed under the wrong species.

speaker: Daniel
text: That noise is one reason we lean on regularisation later in the lecture.

speaker: Samantha
text: Now, the model itself is a small convolutional network with five blocks.

speaker: Samantha
text: Each block has two convolutions, a normalisation layer, and a pooling step.

speaker: Samantha
text: For the optimizer we use Adam, because it is forgiving when the learning rate is not perfectly tuned.

speaker: Samantha
text: Plain stochastic gradient descent can work too, but it needs much more patience.

speaker: Samantha
text: The learning rate warms up over the first two thousand steps and then decays slowly.

speaker: Samantha
text: Without the warm up, the first few hundred updates tend to be wild.

speaker: Daniel
text: Let me add something about memory, because people always run out of it.

speaker: Daniel
text: We train with a batch size of two hundred fifty six on a single graphics card.

speaker: Daniel
text: If your card is smaller, halve the batch and accumulate gradients over two steps.

speaker: Daniel
text: The result is nearly identical, it just takes a little longer.

speaker: Daniel
text: Mixed precision also helps, and it rarely hurts accuracy on a task like this.

speaker: Samantha
text: Next, regularisation, which is where most of the real work happens.

speaker: Samantha
text: We apply dropout with a rate of ten percent after the last two blocks.

speaker: Samantha
text: We also add a little weight decay, which keeps the weights from growing without limit.

speaker: Samantha
text: And we flip and crop the images at random, so the network never sees exactly the same picture twice.

speaker: Samantha
text: Together these tricks matter more than any change to the architecture.

speaker: Daniel
text: Now let us talk about stability, which is the part that usually goes wrong at two in the morning.

speaker: Daniel
text: To stop exploding gradients we use gradient clipping with a maximum norm of one.

speaker: Daniel
text: If you see the loss jump to infinity, check that clipping is switched on before anything else.

speaker: Daniel
text: We also log the gradient norm every hundred steps so problems show up early.

speaker: Samantha
text: So how long do we train? In our runs the validation loss stopped improving after epoch twelve.

speaker: Samantha
text: After that point the training loss keeps falling, but the model is only memorising.

speaker: Samantha
text: That is why we keep the checkpoint with the best validation score, not the last one.

speaker: Daniel
text: One more announcement before we finish.

speaker: Daniel
text: From next week the lab session moves to the Hamilton building, on the second floor.

speaker: Daniel
text: The room is bigger, and there are finally enough power sockets for everyone.

speaker: Samantha
text: And our guest speaker next week works at the European Space Agency, on satellite imaging.

speaker: Samantha
text: Please bring questions, she is happy to talk about careers as well.

speaker: Samantha
text: That is all for today, see you on Thursday.
